content: Initial plan submission for revive-and-verify: bring the stack up on the Mac (db container + native Ollama with nomic-embed-text), re-establish the 287-test baseline (fix the known-broken TestGetStats::test_get_stats_with_data), verify a live store/search/find_related round-trip from Claude Code over MCP, and land doc corrections (README install path, prod env preflight, revival-doc corrections). Plan at docs/phases/revive-and-verify.md. Context: docs/roadmap.md Revival Roadmap section; four decisions locked with human 2026-07-11 (Mac-first, per-agent keys + soft tags, PyPI deprioritized, ambient hooks usage model).

The revive-and-verify phase is directionally sound, but I am requesting changes before approval because this phase commits the new revival roadmap and records several decisions as locked.

1. Add the observed ARM environment repair to Scope, Technical Approach, and Success Criteria. The existing `.venv` is Python 3.12.11 but contains an x86_64 NumPy extension and fails on this ARM Mac before test collection. Recreate the environment with a native ARM Python 3.12, install `.[dev]`, and verify interpreter/package architecture before running pytest. A generic note about dependency drift is not enough for the known first blocker.

2. Align the roadmap with the human's latest stated operating target. Mac-first development is fine, but Windows/WSL2 LAN hosting is the intended personal deployment, not an optional final-phase possibility. Make WSL2 deployment an explicit deliverable and verification target after the daily workflow is proven.

3. Make the daily-driver capture path suggestion-first during development. Session-end capture should propose a checkpoint/status update for confirmation; automatic writes are an end-state capability after trust is established. Reflect this in Phase 10 deliverables and verification.

4. Add the core product direction missing from the revival roadmap: project status/context tracking. At minimum, the roadmap must include canonical per-project status/context, a safe proposed-update workflow, and the eventual ability to update project status after confirmation. The user currently has only scattered notes, so this is central rather than incidental.

5. Include Tagteam explicitly. Tagteam should remain the handoff/review engine while Engram stores or surfaces project continuity. Plan an integration boundary/event flow (for example, ingest approved cycle summaries and use them when proposing project-status updates); do not merge the two systems.

6. Include MCP resources and prompts in the identity/daily workflow design, rather than only hooks, a skill, and an `onboard_agent` tool. Canonical identity/project context fits read-only MCP resources; start-day, switch-project, end-session, and weekly-review workflows fit user-invoked prompts; tools remain appropriate for search and writes.

7. Reconcile or qualify the claimed locked scoping decision. The roadmap currently commits to per-agent keys plus soft tags without a first-class project/workspace model. Per-agent authorization and project organization solve different problems. Preserve the later auth work if desired, but add an explicit decision point for first-class projects/workspaces before treating soft tags as the long-term project model.

8. Update success criterion 5 so the implementation is committed intentionally on the active branch according to the repository workflow; do not require a direct commit to `main` as a technical success criterion.

Keep this phase bounded to revival/verification and documentation corrections. These requests mainly make the plan executable on the current machine and prevent the roadmap/decision log committed by this phase from encoding a product direction that omits the newly agreed daily-use goals.

All 8 requests addressed:

1. ARM env repair — VERIFIED the observation (arm64 interpreter, x86_64 numpy .so in .venv) and added it as explicit Scope item 2, a Technical Approach step (rebuild venv on native ARM Python 3.12, verify arch via `import numpy` before pytest), and Success Criterion 2 in docs/phases/revive-and-verify.md.

2. Windows/WSL2 — reframed in the roadmap preamble and phase doc as the intended personal deployment (not optional); now an explicit deliverable + verification target in Phase 13 (stack running on WSL2 with GPU embeddings, used from the Mac over LAN), scheduled after the daily workflow is proven.

3. Suggestion-first capture — Phase 10 deliverables and Verify now specify session-end capture proposes a checkpoint/status delta for user confirmation before writing; fully automatic capture is documented as the trusted end-state only. Preamble decision wording updated to match.

4. Project status/context tracking — added as the core product direction in the roadmap preamble; Phase 10 gains a v1 proposed-update workflow (propose → confirm → record) with a Verify criterion; Phase 11 gains canonical per-project status/context files.

5. Tagteam integration — Phase 11 deliverable: ingest approved cycle summaries into engram and use them as evidence for proposed status updates; boundary stated explicitly (tagteam stays the handoff/review engine, systems not merged). Also in the preamble.

6. MCP resources + prompts — Phase 11: identity and project status/context exposed as read-only MCP resources; Phase 10: MCP prompts for start-day, switch-project, end-session, weekly-review. Tools remain for search/writes.

7. Scoping decision qualified — preamble and phase doc now separate per-agent authorization (locked) from the long-term project model (open); Phase 12's first deliverable is an explicit decision checkpoint on first-class projects/workspaces informed by daily-driver usage, logged to the decision log before implementation.

8. Success criterion — reworded (now criterion 6): commit intentionally on the active branch per repository workflow; no requirement to commit directly to main.

Phase scope remains revival/verification + doc corrections only. Files changed: docs/phases/revive-and-verify.md, docs/roadmap.md.

Approved. The revised plan is executable on the current ARM Mac and the committed revival roadmap now reflects suggestion-first capture, canonical project status/context, a clear Tagteam integration boundary, MCP resources/prompts, an explicit project-model decision checkpoint, and Windows/WSL2 as the intended deployment target.
